title: Issue Triage Proposal
eyebrow: Proposal for issue #162 · nothing closed or changed on GitHub yet

short.lead: I checked all 47 open Focus Deck issues against every commit on main, every merged pull request and all 77 closed issues. Ten issues are already done or duplicated and only wait for you to test and close them. Of the other 37, 28 fall into seven bursts of work (each one branch and one pull request), 8 are ideas for later, and one is this triage issue (#162).
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes and what it needs from you. The full write-up is docs/plans/issue-triage-2026-10-15.md on the branch AjsAgent/recent-triaging-issue-suw0wn.
items: A cross-check of every open issue against commits on main, merged pull requests and closed issue titles. Older issues were also checked against the current code under app/.
Nothing changes until you have tested. Open the Board from the rail and tick, drag and swipe a card. Then set a task due tomorrow and check it shows yellow.
About five minutes in the app, on a phone and on a wide screen.
I close the ten finished issues

The Board (#140 and #142 to #147), "Due dates: colour stages" (#107) and "Fix due dates not quite working" (#114) close as completed, each with a comment linking its merged pull request. "Make reminder tasks schedulable" (#69) closes as a duplicate of "Due dates: in-app reminders" (#111).
Your answer to the first choice below.
I set up one parent issue per burst

Seven parent issues, Burst A to Burst G, each with its issues attached as sub-issues. The roadmap is updated to match, which also removes #46 ("grill me on the usability and readability") because it is already closed.
Your answer to the second choice below.
I start Burst A: never lose what you're writing

A fix so an open editor counts as a draft and is saved before a sync or a click-away can replace it. This covers "Syncing overwrites a thought mid-write" (#155) and "Clicking off a new task with steps discards it" (#157).
Your approval of the bursts, and later a test of the fix.

Burst A: never lose what you're writing
#155 Syncing overwrites text mid-write; #157 Clicking off a new task with steps discards it.
One fix covers both: treat an open editor as a draft, and save it before anything can replace it. It touches app/js/app.js and app/js/merge.js. This burst goes first because it loses your data.
A sync or a click-away can wipe text you are typing.
Open editors are saved as drafts first.
Nothing you are writing is lost.

Burst B: GitHub sync bugs
#93 issues not pulled in; #94 same-number issue ignored; #102 moving between repos silently does nothing.

All three are in app/js/github-sync.js and app/js/github.js. This is two pull requests: one for #93 and #94 (pulling issues in), then one for #102 (moving a task between repos), which must also show an error when the move fails.
Issues go missing, or a move silently fails.

Your GitHub issues and your deck stay in step.

Burst D: adding and editing tasks
#158 steps shown as "3 of 5 done" with a tidier editor; #156 make the Cancel button smaller; #161 pick several categories quickly; #103 add a task from a single field.
#158 is the largest. The other three go in the same pull request or straight after it.

Burst E: Focus and Sort polish

#74 show Back instead of Clear; #76 the Done step in the Sort flow; #96 Focus follows the open project; #89 Surprise me across several projects; #151 the "Filed to X" message fades after 5 seconds; #159 edit tray notes after filing.

The focus card still says Clear (app/js/render.js:204). Surprise me already works for one project through the project wallet, the row of project cards on the Focus screen, but not for several. The side rail from PR #134 may already cover the part of #76 about switching between Sort and Focus, so I will check that first.
Several small rough edges in Focus and Sort.
Six small fixes in one pull request.
Focus and Sort feel finished.

Burst F: the rest of the due-dates plan
#108 red tasks rise to the top, #109 time of day, #110 repeating tasks, #111 in-app reminders, #112 phone notifications.

The parent issue, "Due-date colour stages, repeating tasks and configurable reminders" (#106), and its plan in docs/plans/due-dates-and-repeats.md already set this order. The bursts keep it unchanged, with one pull request each.
new

"Fix focus deck UI not being proper" (#150) has no description, so I cannot build it yet. "Make it warmer, like a leather-edged notebook" (#87) may already have been answered by the desk redesign in PR #127.
Three look-and-feel issues, two of them unclear.
A completion bar fix, then the other two once you have answered.
The app looks the way you want.
